instrument_name: 19 Del. C. ch. 9 Minimum Wage Act (901-914)
figure_or_rule_carried: State minimum wage 15.00/h effective 2025-01-01 (902(a)(5)); last statutory step, no indexation and no 2027 step in the text; becomes the federal rate if federal exceeds it. Tipped: tip credit = federal tip-credit percentage as of 2006-06-15 of the state minimum, cash wage never below 2.23/h (902(b)); tipped occupation = customarily >30/month in tips (902(c)(1)); tips are the employee's property, employer-mandated pool max 15% of primary direct-service employee's tips (902(d)(2)). Excluded from 'employee' (901(3)): agriculture, domestic service in a private home, bona fide EAP and outside sales, US government employees, gratuitous nonprofit volunteers, fishing/first processing at sea, under-18 summer camp counselors, DOC inmates (unless private employer), minor-league baseball under CBA. Records 3 years: name, address, occupation, rate, amount paid each period, hours each day and week (907).

instrument_name: 19 Del. C. ch. 11 Wage Payment and Collection Act (1101-1115)
figure_or_rule_carried: Coverage: private employers; excludes US, State of Delaware and political subdivisions (1101(4)-(5)). Pay at least once per calendar month on paydays designated in advance; within 7 days of the close of the pay period; nonwork payday -> preceding workday; overtime/new hires/variable part-timers may slip to next period if pay period <= 16 days and payday within period (1102(a)-(b)). Direct deposit only on the employee's written request (1102(a)). Final pay: on quit, discharge, suspension or layoff wages due on the LATER of the next regular payday or 3 business days after the last day worked, usual channel or by mail on request (1103(a)); liquidated damages lower of 10%/day or the unpaid wages (1103(b)(2)). Deductions only if required by law, for medical care without employer benefit, or with signed employee authorization for a lawful purpose for the employee's benefit (1107). Employers of over 3 employees: written notice at hire of rate and day/hour/place of payment; pay statement at time of payment on the check, a separate slip or electronically if retainable, showing wages due, pay period, total deductions separately specified, and hours for hourly employees; employee may request paper; records 3 years (1108). Benefits/wage supplements (incl. vacation, separation pay) payable within 30 days after due under the agreement (1109). Wage theft 1102A: failure to withhold taxes or forward withholding within 7 days of the pay period is a violation, civil penalty 2,000-20,000 per violation.

instrument_name: 30 Del. C. ch. 11 subch. I-II Personal Income Tax: rates, residence, standard deduction, personal credit, credit for tax paid to another state
figure_or_rule_carried: Rates for taxable years after 2013-12-31 (still in force 2026, no later paragraph enacted): 0% to 2,000; 2.2% 2,000-5,000; 3.9% 5,000-10,000; 4.8% 10,000-20,000; 5.2% 20,000-25,000; 5.55% 25,000-60,000; 6.6% over 60,000 (1102(a)(14)). Resident = domiciled, or abode in DE and >183 days (1103). Standard deduction 3,250 single / 6,500 joint / 3,250 each MFS (1108(a)(3)), +2,500 for 65+ or blind (1108(b)). Personal credit 110 per federal personal exemption, +110 if 60 or over, not exceeding tax (1110(b)-(c)). Resident credit for income tax paid to another state on income sourced there, limited by DE tax x other-state taxable income / entire taxable income (1111) - operates at ASSESSMENT. Not indexed.

instrument_name: 30 Del. C. 1121-1124 Nonresident individuals: tax and Delaware-source income
figure_or_rule_carried: Nonresident tax = resident-basis tax under 1102 less 1110(b) credit, times modified DE-source income / DE AGI (1121). Employee compensation is DE-source if for services (a) rendered in DE or (b) attributable to employment in DE and not required to be performed elsewhere (1124(b)(1)) - the statutory basis of Delaware's convenience-of-the-employer rule (employer-necessity test). Armed-forces pay of nonresidents excluded (1124(g)).

instrument_name: 30 Del. C. 1151-1156A Withholding, W-2, returns, deposit frequency, new hires
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer with an office or business in DE withholds from resident or nonresident wages taxable under ch. 11 when the wages are subject to federal withholding; method/tables prescribed by the Division (1151(a)); employee has the same number of exemptions as for federal purposes, employer may rely on the federal count (1151(b)); reciprocity agreements authorised but none in force (1151(c); FAQ US-DE-WH-001). W-2 to employee by Jan 31, or within 30 days of last wage payment on termination (1152). Filing frequency by July-June lookback: quarterly <= 4,500, monthly 4,500-25,000 (or no DE employees in lookback), eighth-monthly > 25,000, thresholds indexed under 30 Del. C. 515 (1154(a)); quarterly due last day of month after quarter; monthly by the 15th of next month; eighth-monthly 3 working days after periods ending 3rd, 7th, 11th, 15th, 19th, 22nd, 25th, last day (1154(c)-(e)); EFT if federal EFT required, with 1-year lag (1154(g)); W-2/1099 information returns to the Division by Jan 31, in machine-readable form when required federally (1154(i)). Withheld tax is a trust fund (1155). New hires to the State Directory of New Hires within 20 days (or 2 monthly electronic transmissions 12-16 days apart; multistate employer may designate one state): name, address, SSN, first day of paid service, employer name, address, FEIN, on W-4 or equivalent; rehire after 60+ days separation counts; fine 25 per failure, 500 for conspiracy (1156A). 1154 last amended by 85 Del. Laws c. 301 (content of the amendment not identified).

instrument_name: Delaware Division of Revenue Employer's Guide - Withholding Regulations and Employer Duties (live page)
figure_or_rule_carried: Live page text identical to the 2026-10-13 Wayback copy of US-DE-P5-1-003. Annualized method: annualize gross (daily x300, weekly x52, monthly x12, semi-monthly x24, biweekly x26); minus standard deduction 3,250 single / 6,500 MFJ / 3,250 MFS; tax by table 'Effective January 1, 2025': 0-2,000 0; 2,000-5,000 0 + 2.2%; 5,000-10,000 66 + 3.9%; 10,000-20,000 261 + 4.8%; 20,000-25,000 741 + 5.2%; 25,000-60,000 1,001 + 5.55%; 60,000+ 2,943.50 + 6.6%; minus 110 x personal exemptions; divide by pay periods. Worked example single 1 allowance 25,000 annual: tax 832.00 - 110 = 722.00; weekly 13.88, biweekly 27.77, semi-monthly 30.08, monthly 60.17. Supplemental paid separately: annualized-with minus annualized-without (example 500/wk + 5,000 bonus single 1 allowance: withhold 269.63); paid with regular wages: one payment. Tips as supplemental. Certificate: federal W-4 (text still says W-4/W-4A and allowances; DE worksheet forms SD/W-4A, W-4NR for nonresidents); no certificate -> single, no allowances. Copies to the Division within 5 working days if 14+ allowances or exempt with wages expected > 168.50/week. No explicit rounding rule (examples round to cents).

instrument_name: Delaware Withholding Tax Due Dates for Calendar Year 2026
figure_or_rule_carried: 2026 calendar: monthly filers due 02/17, 03/16, 04/15, 05/15, 06/15, 07/15, 08/17, 09/15, 10/15, 11/16, 12/15/2026 and 01/15/2027; eighth-monthly periods end 3rd, 7th, 11th, 15th, 19th, 22nd, 25th and last day, each due about 3 working days later (e.g. period ending 01/03/26 due 01/07/26, 01/31/26 due 02/04/26); quarterly filers listed in the same table. Electronic transactions must start at least one day before the due date; tax type code 01106 (withholding).

instrument_name: Delaware Division of Revenue Withholding Tax FAQs and W-2 and 1099 Form FAQs
article_or_section: Withholding Tax FAQs (https://revenue.delaware.gov/business-tax-forms/withholding-tax/); W-2 and 1099 FAQs (all Q&A)
figure_or_rule_carried: Registration via One Stop Business Licensing and Registration; returns filed/paid on https://tax.delaware.gov/ (paper booklets no longer mailed); new withholding agents file monthly until the next lookback; no consolidated payments across FEINs; federal W-4 accepted; no reciprocity with any state, withholding only in the duty state, DE residents get a credit at assessment; deferred compensation: recommended withholding 5%; late filing 5%/month + 0.5%/month interest + 1%/month (max 25%) failure to pay (30 Del. C. 533-534). W-2: TY2025 due 2026-02-02 paper and electronic (same as federal); online via Delaware Taxpayer Portal or bulk upload, paper only for 10 or fewer W-2/1099-R; EFW2 file accepted only if it contains Delaware RS records; do NOT truncate SSN on W-2 Copy 1 or in the RS record; W-2c/W-3c paper only; Form WTH-REC replaces federal W-3 (one per EIN); 1099-MISC/NEC for DE residents or nonresidents working in DE and 1099-R with DE withholding reported directly (Pub 1220, B record positions 663-684 state code and payer ID); W-2 data file spec is in the FAQ document on the Delaware Tax Portal (not read).

instrument_name: Delaware Form WTH-REC Annual Reconciliation instructions (Revised 02/03/26)
figure_or_rule_carried: WTH-REC Annual Reconciliation/Transmittal due on or before the last day of January with a duplicate of each W-2; employers required to e-file W-2/1099 federally must e-file for Delaware; include only employees with Delaware wages; penalty half the IRC amounts. Fields: business name, taxpayer ID, e-file checkbox, change-form checkbox, tax period start/end, Line 1 total Delaware wages, Line 2 number of W-2s/1099s, Line 3 DE tax withheld (worksheet), Line 4 DE tax paid, Line 5 difference (5a balance due / 5b overpayment with explanation; no carryover; no employer refund where tax was withheld, 30 Del. C. 537). Monthly worksheet of tax withheld and paid.

instrument_name: 19 Del. C. ch. 33 subch. I Unemployment Compensation - definitions (3302): taxable wage base, localization, exclusions
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wage base: 12,500 for 2025; 14,500 from 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31; 16,500 after 2026-12-31 (or the FUTA base if higher) (3302(28)(A)(vii)-(ix)); the older trust-fund-tiered 18,500/16,500/14,500 rule in (vi) is displaced for these years by the dated paragraphs (DOL FAQ still prints 18,500 and 10,500: stale). 3302(28)(A)(x): for the wage-base computation 'employment' includes service covered by another state's UI law -> wages paid by the same employer and reported to another state in the year count toward the DE 14,500. Localization: entire service covered if localized in DE, or not localized anywhere with base/direction/control or residence tests (3302(12)(H)-(I)). Excluded employment (3302(15)): agricultural labor unless employer paid 20,000+ cash in a quarter or had 10+ workers in 20 weeks; domestic service unless 1,000+ cash in a quarter; service for one's child or spouse and child under 18 for a parent; state/political subdivision (except as in (14)(B)); 501(c)(3)-type organizations as stated (reimbursement election exists); officers of social clubs/unions etc.; commission-only insurance and real estate agents; students employed by their school; work-study students; hospital patients; elected/appointed officials; direct sellers (IRC 3508). Retirement, sickness/disability, medical and death plan payments excluded from wages (28)(B).

instrument_name: Delaware DOL Division of Unemployment Insurance - Employer FAQs (live)
article_or_section: Q: How are my tax rates determined; Q: Operations & Technology Tax; Q: How does my business file quarterly reports
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly UI: Forms UC-8 (tax report) and UC-8A (wage report) each quarter, gross and taxable wages, due by the end of the month after the quarter with payment; late: interest 1.5%/month and 17.50 penalty per late report; magnetic/electronic media accepted (contact unit). Rates: new employer rate = average rate of all employers over the last five years; construction employers headquartered elsewhere get the average construction rate; earned rate after two fiscal years (basic rate from benefit ratio + supplemental assessment); delinquent (penalty) rate; transfer of experience; rate notices issued in January. Operations & Technology tax 0.2%: now separated out of the contributory rate and billed by letter (August 2026); 2026 Q1 due 2026-08-31, Q2 due 2026-09-30, Q3/Q4 by later letters; paid by check to 'Op & Tech Lockbox'. Liability: agricultural 20,000/quarter or 10 workers in 20 weeks; domestic 1,000/quarter; corporate officers covered. Page still prints wage base 18,500 and 10,500: stale, statute governs (US-DES5-010). 2026 new-employer rate figure NOT on the page.

instrument_name: 19 Del. C. ch. 37 Healthy Delaware Families Act (Delaware Paid Leave): coverage, contributions, benefits
figure_or_rule_carried: Statutory contribution rates for 2025 AND 2026: medical 0.40%, family caregiving 0.08%, parental 0.32% of wages (3705(b)(1)-(3)); from 2027 set annually by the Department on actuarial principles, total capped at 1.00% (above that, benefit % is cut) (3705(b),(c)). Employer may deduct NOT MORE than 50% of each contribution from the employee, may pay more; deduction only concurrent with and proportionate to wages paid; employer liable for the full amount if not deducted (3705(d)-(g)). Remittance quarterly or as the Department regulates (3705(b)). Waiver form where schedule/tenure won't meet eligibility (3705(k)). Wages = FICA wages (3701(24)) -> capped at the Social Security wage base. Employer coverage (3701(7)): 10-24 employees in previous 12 months = parental leave only (0.32%); 25+ = all three (0.80%); fewer than 10 not covered (voluntary). Employee = primarily reporting for work at a DE worksite; out-of-state worksite employees excluded unless the employer elects (3701(6)a) -> multistate coverage follows the primary worksite, not UI localization. Covered individual: 12 months and 1,250 hours with the employer (3701(3)). Benefits: 80% of average weekly wage, min 100, max 900/week in 2026 and 2027, then CPI-U Philadelphia-Camden-Wilmington indexed (3704(a)); 12 weeks parental per application year; 6 weeks medical/caregiving per 24 months (3703). Claimant told benefits may be taxable; taxes withheld per regulation (3714). Supersedes the tier-B levy row US-DEP7-002 for the rate (now statute-backed).

instrument_name: Delaware DOL - Delaware Paid Leave Employers page (live)
article_or_section: Am I required to participate; Key Dates
figure_or_rule_carried: Exempt: employers with nine or fewer employees (may opt in), federal government employers, seasonal operations closed to the public a month or more. Key dates: deductions from 2025-01-01; first quarterly Hours & Wage Report due 2025-04-30; Q1-Q2 2025 contributions due 2025-07-30; claims from 2026-01-01. Filing in Delaware LaborFirst portal. Notice of Employee Rights (English and Spanish) to be given when coverage begins. No 2027 contribution rate published on the page as of 2026-11-02.

instrument_name: 10 Del. C. 4913 Exemption and attachment of wages
figure_or_rule_carried: 85% of the wages of any person residing in Delaware is exempt from mesne and execution attachment (so creditor garnishment max 15% of wages, vs CCPA 25% of disposable earnings - apply the more protective of the two per pay period); the 85% limit does not apply to process for fines, costs or taxes owed to the State. Only one attachment at a time on any amount of wages due; first attaching creditor has priority until paid in full. Wages include salaries, commissions and every other remuneration for services (not self-employment). Base is 'wages' (gross wording), not 'disposable earnings' - the comparison with CCPA must be done per payment.

instrument_name: 29 Del. C. 6960 Prevailing wage requirements (public works)
figure_or_rule_carried: Applies to State or subdivision public works contracts with State funds over 500,000 (new construction incl. painting/decorating) or 45,000 (alteration, repair, renovation, demolition, reconstruction). Rates set by DOL; CBA rates adopted where they prevailed 4 of last 5 years, raise per CBA as of September 1. Laborers and mechanics paid unconditionally at least WEEKLY, no deductions or rebates beyond lawful ones; sworn payroll information furnished WEEKLY as required by DOL (certified payroll), retained by DOL 6 months; civil penalty 1,000-5,000 per violation incl. failure to submit payroll reports or post the rates; treble damages; not applicable to DOT Community Transportation Fund or Municipal Street Aid projects.

instrument_name: 13 Del. C. 513 Judgment; order of support; income withholding and employer duties
figure_or_rule_carried: Support attachments are not subject to the 10 Del. C. 4913 85% exemption; limited by CCPA 303(b) (15 U.S.C. 1673(b)); priority over every other attachment except federal tax liens, regardless of date (513(b)(7)). Arrears add-on: current support plus up to 20% of current support or 20/month, whichever greater, where no arrears payment ordered or it is below 20% (513(b)(2)b). Employer deducts the specified sum and may deduct a State-established fee unless it waives it (amount NOT stated in the statute); remit at or before payday; start no later than 7 days after the first payday following receipt; remittance shows obligor name and SSN; one combined payment allowed to DCSS; for another state's IWO apply the law of the obligor's principal place of employment for 411(d) factors (513(b)(8)a). Employers with 50+ employees must remit to DCSS by EFT/EDI (513(b)(8)b). Notify court/DCSS of termination with last address and new employer; NMSN to plan within 20 business days. Penalties: up to 1,000 / 90 days first offense for non-compliance or dismissal due to attachment, up to 5,000 thereafter (513(b)(10)); 100-500 fine for not answering a DCSS information request within 30 days (513(f)).

instrument_name: 19 Del. C. ch. 5 Child Labor (501-509)
figure_or_rule_carried: Minors (under 18) may not be employed unless the employer holds a verified and validated employment certificate (work permit) on file and available to DOL (504(a)); issued by school district designees or DOL (504(b)). Under 14, under 16 and under 18 occupational and hours restrictions (505-507); under-18 prohibited occupations include FLSA hazardous orders, blast furnaces, docks, railroads, electrical wiring, distilleries, toxic chemicals. Minimum wage: no youth sub-minimum in 19 Del. C. ch. 9 (minors get 15.00). Payroll impact: HR data item 'work permit on file' for employees under 18.

instrument_name: 30 Del. C. 1105-1106 Taxable income = federal AGI with Delaware modifications (conformity)
figure_or_rule_carried: Resident taxable income = federal adjusted gross income 'as the same are or shall become effective for any taxable year' with the ch. 11 modifications (1105) -> rolling conformity: federal wage exclusions (401(k)/403(b)/457 deferrals, section 125 cafeteria plan, HSA, qualified transportation fringes, group-term life up to 50,000, other IRC exclusions) flow through to Delaware wages; no HSA or 125 add-back found in 1106 (modifications concern US obligation interest, other-state bond interest, pension exclusion 2,000 / 12,500 at 60+, disability exclusion, military pension 12,500 -> 15,000 from TY2027 etc., i.e. assessment-level items, not payroll). Withholding base = wages subject to federal withholding (1151(a)) -> state taxable wages = federal FIT wages.

instrument_name: 6 Del. C. ch. 12B Computer Security Breaches (12B-100 to 12B-104)
figure_or_rule_carried: Any person conducting business in DE that owns/licenses/maintains personal information (incl. SSN) must implement reasonable security procedures (12B-100); breach notice to residents without unreasonable delay and within 60 days of determination (12B-102(c)); notice to the Attorney General if more than 500 residents (12B-102(d)); if SSNs are breached, 1 year of free credit monitoring (12B-102(e)). No Delaware statute restricting SSN display on pay statements was located (searched Delaware Code and the web 2026-11-02); 19 Del. C. 1108(4) pay-statement content does not include the SSN. W-2 state copy and EFW2 RS record must carry the full 9-digit SSN (US-DES5-008).

instrument_name: Delaware DOL Division of Industrial Affairs - Employer Knowledgebase (minimum wage, tipped cash wage, days off)
authority: Delaware Department of Labor, Division of Industrial Affairs
figure_or_rule_carried: Future increases: the KB names only the 15.00/h step of 2025-01-01 (no later increase announced; consistent with 19 Del. C. 902).
